newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Three African states get loans worth $59.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Three African states get loans worth $59.5 mln.

text.p: The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved loans to Zambia, Senegal and Ivory Coast respectively for agriculture, education, and rural water projects totalling $59.5 million, a bank statement said.
The Zambian loan for $22 million will help the southern African country's programme of investment in agriculture.
The objective is to help raise Gross Domestic Product and incomes of farming households and improve mobility and access to information on markets and prices, the statement added.
The programme covers development of vegetable and livestock production, support in research, training and infrastructure development and extension of credit structures in rural Zambia.

The Senegal credit, from the bank's soft-loan arm, African Development Fund, is for $17.5 million. It will help finance the second phase of Senegal's education project, with emphasis on increasing access to education and improving teaching and teachers. The loan is for 50 years with a 10-year grace.

The AfDB board of governors also approved a loan of $20 million for the development of rural water schemes in Ivory Coast. It is also repayable in 50 years with 10 years of grace. -- Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
